correctness.rationale: The non-atomic support-perfectness argument forces any affine relation between Gini and variance first projections to have a strictly positive coefficient and an affine CDF on a connected bounded support, hence uniform. Direct overlapping-pair covariance yields all three exact finite moments, including contrast variance 1/[90n(n-1)]. The exact Bernoulli-polynomial representation equates the contrast with a centered Watson statistic for every sample. A Fourier CLT with uniform summable tail proves the weighted chi-square limit, whose variance is 1/90. The checker passed 56,331 deterministic rational and numerical Fourier assertions; it is supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Older primary work supplies general U-statistic methods, uniform Gini efficiency and maximal rank-correlation relationships, but the inspected claims do not entail the all-atomless iff characterization of perfect estimator alignment or the exact Gini-minus-variance Watson identity. Comparison is by implication: the 2003 maximum-correlation criterion applies to a different correlation, and 2014 equal efficiency is only a one-way statement. Priority remains qualified by partially inaccessible older literature.
residual_risks: A differently named full iff result may occur in older distribution-characterization literature.
The original Watson (1961) and the 2004 Gini-variance estimator paper were not fully accessible, and visual inspection of the 2003 PDF was unavailable despite a full text extraction.
The known-support contrast identity is unsuitable for estimating unknown uniform endpoints without new calibration.

value.rationale: The result resolves the natural complete classification of distributions for which two widely used scale estimators share all first-order fluctuation; this distinguishes the uniform law from arbitrary non-atomic alternatives. The exact n-dependent correlation and rigorous second-order Watson link explain what is left after first-order cancellation, making a precise goodness-of-fit interpretation useful. Neither standard U-statistic correctness nor generic uniform efficiency alone establishes this classification.
